claims.statement: Monthly variable payroll input must be submitted by the 5th working day of the following month.
claims.quote: Monthly variable input (overtime, bonuses, absences) must reach us by the 5th working day of the following month.

claims.statement: The Dimona IN declaration must be filed no later than the start date of the employee.
claims.value: no later than the start date
claims.quote: The Dimona IN declaration must be filed no later than the moment the employee starts working.

claims.statement: Employees have no right to request pay information about colleagues, either individually or as averages.
claims.quote: Employees have no right to receive any information about the pay of other employees, not individually and not as an average.

claims.statement: Employees are bound by strict confidentiality regarding salary information.
claims.quote: Salary information is strictly confidential.

claims.statement: Internal staff with a structural telework agreement may work from home up to three days per week.
claims.quote: Staff with a structural telework agreement may work from home up to three days per week.

claims.statement: Internal staff working from home at least two days per week receive a monthly home-office allowance of EUR 140.
claims.quote: Staff working from home at least two days per week receive a monthly home-office allowance of EUR 140, paid with the monthly salary.

claims.statement: Employers are prohibited from asking job applicants about their current or previous salary.
claims.quote: Employers may not ask job applicants about their pay history in current or previous employment (Art. 5(2)).

claims.statement: Job applicants must be informed about the initial pay or its range before the job interview.
claims.quote: Applicants must receive information about the initial pay or its range, based on objective, gender-neutral criteria, before the job interview (Art. 5(1)).

claims.statement: Employers cannot enforce contractual terms that prevent employees from disclosing their own pay.
claims.quote: Contractual terms that prevent workers from disclosing their own pay are not allowed (Art. 7(5)).

claims.statement: Employees have the right to request their individual pay level and average pay levels by sex for comparable workers.
claims.value: own pay and averages by sex
claims.quote: Workers may request information on their individual pay level and on the average pay levels, broken down by sex, for categories of workers doing the same work or work of equal value (Art. 7(1)).

claims.statement: Employers must respond to employee pay information requests within two months at the latest.
claims.quote: The employer must answer within a reasonable period, and at the latest within two months (Art. 7(4)).

claims.statement: Employers with 250 or more workers must publish a gender pay gap report annually starting 7 June 2027.
claims.quote: 250 or more workers: first gender pay gap report by 7 June 2027, then every year.

claims.statement: A joint pay assessment with worker representatives is required if an unexplained gender pay gap of 5% or more persists for six months.
claims.quote: A joint pay assessment with worker representatives is required when the gap in any category is 5% or more, is not justified by objective gender-neutral criteria, and is not remedied within six months (Art. 10).

claims.statement: Employees do not have the right to access the individual pay information of a named colleague.
claims.quote: Individual pay of a named colleague is not part of this right.

claims.statement: For cross-border workers, the 25% threshold in the country of residence must be checked to determine social security applicability and an A1 must be requested.
claims.quote: check the 25% threshold in the country of residence, then request an A1.

claims.statement: Wage tax for cross-border workers depends on tax treaties and the current tolerance for home-working days, which must be verified before advising clients.
claims.quote: look at the treaty and at the tolerance for home-working days, which changes regularly, so check the current number with me before telling the client anything.

claims.statement: Recruiters may not ask candidates about their current or previous salary.
claims.quote: your recruiters should no longer ask candidates about their current or previous salary.

claims.statement: Candidates must be told the pay range or starting pay before the interview.
claims.quote: you need to share the pay range, or the starting pay, before the interview, not at offer stage.

claims.statement: Employees cannot be bound to keep their own pay confidential in employment contracts.
claims.quote: the confidentiality clause on salary (article 9 in the 2022 template) can no longer be enforced

claims.statement: The monthly home-office allowance for staff with a structural telework agreement is EUR 150 as of 1 January 2026.
claims.quote: the monthly home-office allowance increases from EUR 140 to EUR 150 for all staff with a structural telework agreement

claims.statement: Staff with a structural telework agreement are eligible for the home-office allowance.
claims.quote: for all staff with a structural telework agreement

claims.statement: The Dimona IN declaration must be submitted at the latest when the employee starts work.
claims.quote: Submit the Dimona IN declaration at the latest at the moment the employee starts work.

claims.statement: The signed employment contract must be received before onboarding the employee.
claims.quote: Receive the signed employment contract.

claims.statement: The bank account number and a copy of the ID card must be collected during onboarding.
claims.quote: Collect the bank account number and a copy of the ID card.

claims.statement: The joint committee and matching wage scale must be verified during onboarding.
claims.quote: Check the joint committee (paritair comite) of the client and the matching wage scale.

claims.statement: The employee must be created in mysdworx and sent a self-service invitation during onboarding.
claims.quote: Create the employee in mysdworx and send the self-service invitation.

claims.statement: Recruiters may ask candidates about their current gross monthly salary during the first interview.
claims.quote: Always ask the candidate for their current gross monthly salary and benefits package during the first interview.

claims.statement: Candidates must be told the salary range only after an offer is made.
claims.quote: Salary ranges are shared only once an offer is made.

claims.statement: Salary ranges must not be published in job adverts or discussed in the first interview.
claims.quote: Never publish a range in the job advert or discuss it in the first interview, so you keep room to negotiate.

claims.statement: Belgian social security applies if 25% or more of working time or pay is in Belgium.
claims.quote: First check whether 25% or more of working time or pay is in the country of residence, so Belgium. If yes, Belgian social security applies to all of it

claims.statement: An A1 certificate must be requested through the Belgian institution when Belgian social security applies.
claims.quote: you request an A1 certificate through the Belgian institution

claims.statement: Wage tax for cross-border workers is split by working days under the Belgium-Netherlands tax treaty.
claims.quote: Wage tax is a separate question and is split by working days under the BE-NL treaty

claims.statement: A cross-border worker from the Netherlands working 100% in Belgium is subject to Belgian social security.
claims.quote: If all work is physically done in Belgium, yes: Belgian social security and Belgian wage tax.

claims.statement: A cross-border worker from the Netherlands working 100% in Belgium is subject to Belgian wage tax.
claims.quote: If all work is physically done in Belgium, yes: Belgian social security and Belgian wage tax.

claims.statement: The 25% threshold rule applies again if a cross-border worker starts working from home in the Netherlands.
claims.quote: It only gets complicated once they start working from home in NL. Then the 25% check applies again.

claims.statement: Changes in telework arrangements for cross-border workers must be flagged in the file for review.
claims.quote: Flag it in the file so we see it when the telework agreement changes.

claims.statement: The deadline for submitting monthly variable payroll input is the 3rd working day.
claims.quote: Payroll Ops confirms the cut-off is the 3rd working day since February.

claims.statement: Employees are required to keep their remuneration and benefits confidential and not disclose them to colleagues or third parties.
claims.quote: The Employee shall keep the amount of their remuneration and benefits strictly confidential and shall not disclose them to colleagues or third parties.

claims.statement: Monthly variable payroll input for Dutch payrolls must be submitted by the 5th working day of the following month.
claims.quote: must be submitted by the 5th working day of the following month

claims.statement: Variable payroll input must be submitted by the 3rd working day of the following month at 12:00 CET.
claims.quote: must be submitted in mysdworx by the 3rd working day of the following month, 12:00 CET.

issues.title: Employee self-service FAQ: can I find out what my colleagues earn? contradicts LW-2026-041
issues.explanation: FAQ-ESS-117 states employees have no right to request average pay, while LW-2026-041 grants the right to request average pay by sex for comparable workers. FAQ-ESS-117 was last reviewed on 2024-10-01, before the rule took effect on 2026-06-07.
issues.suggested_fix: Employees have the right to request their individual pay level and the average pay levels by sex for comparable workers.

issues.title: Employee self-service FAQ: can I find out what my colleagues earn? contradicts LW-2026-041
issues.explanation: One states pay confidentiality is strictly enforced, the other says employers cannot enforce such restrictions. FAQ-ESS-117 was last reviewed on 2024-10-01, before the rule took effect on 2026-06-07.
issues.suggested_fix: Salary information is personal and confidential, but employees are free to discuss their own pay. You may not access or share others' salary details without authorization.

issues.title: Employment contract template, white-collar, Belgium (v2022) contradicts LW-2026-041
issues.explanation: One prohibits enforcing pay confidentiality, the other requires it in contracts. TPL-CONTRACT-BE-WC was last reviewed on 2022-11-02, before the rule took effect on 2026-06-07.
issues.suggested_fix: The Employee has the right to disclose their own remuneration and benefits, in accordance with applicable law. Such disclosure may be made to colleagues, third parties, or other individuals, particularly to discuss or address matters related to pay transparency.

issues.title: Recruitment playbook for client HR teams contradicts LW-2026-041
issues.explanation: LW-2026-041 prohibits asking about salary, while PB-REC-2023 allows it during the first interview. PB-REC-2023 was last reviewed on 2023-03-14, before the rule took effect on 2026-06-07.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not ask candidates about their current or previous salary or benefits during any stage of the interview process.

issues.title: Recruitment playbook for client HR teams contradicts LW-2026-041
issues.explanation: One requires pay disclosure before the interview, the other mandates it only after an offer. PB-REC-2023 was last reviewed on 2023-03-14, before the rule took effect on 2026-06-07.
issues.suggested_fix: Salary ranges must be communicated to job applicants prior to the interview stage.

issues.title: FAQ-CLIENT-DEADLINES and WIKI-PAYOPS-CUTOFF disagree
issues.explanation: Different values: "5th working day" vs "3rd working day". WIKI-PAYOPS-CUTOFF (2026-02-10) says "3rd working day", FAQ-CLIENT-DEADLINES (2025-01-20) says "5th working day". The older source is probably stale; it has no owner, so this goes to Koen Wouters, who owns the newer source.

issues.title: HR-POLICY-HOMEOFFICE and NEWS-2026-01-HOMEOFFICE disagree
issues.explanation: Different values: "EUR 140" vs "EUR 150". NEWS-2026-01-HOMEOFFICE (2026-01-08) says "EUR 150", HR-POLICY-HOMEOFFICE (2024-01-15) says "EUR 140". The older source is probably stale; its owner confirms.

issues.title: No official source for: Which social security applies to cross-border workers, A1, 25% threshold
issues.explanation: 3 informal answers in chats and mails, 3 of them by Jonas Verbeke. No wiki page, FAQ or policy covers this.
issues.suggested_fix:
- For cross-border workers, social security and wage tax are separate issues.
- Apply EU multi-state rules for social security: if 25% or more of work time or pay is in the country of residence, that country's social security applies fully.
- In such cases, request an A1 certificate via the institution of the residence country.
- Wage tax follows the tax treaty (e.g., BE-NL) and may split liability based on working days; current home-working tolerances change regularly.
- Always check with Jonas before advising clients on wage tax.
- Log all cases with Jonas; no official article exists yet.
- Flag cases where telework could change the 25% assessment.

issues.title: No official source for: How wage tax is handled for cross-border workers
issues.explanation: 3 informal answers in chats and mails, 3 of them by Jonas Verbeke. No wiki page, FAQ or policy covers this.
issues.suggested_fix:
- Cross-border workers involve two issues: social security and wage tax
- For social security: if 25% or more of work time or pay is in the country of residence, that country covers all; request A1 certificate
- Wage tax follows the BE-NL treaty and depends on where work is performed
- Home-working days tolerance changes; always check current rules with expert
- Flag cases with potential telework changes
- Log all cases with Jonas; no official article available yet
- Check with the expert: current home-working days tolerance
